identity.title: VibeVoice: Expressive Podcast Generation with Next-Token Diffusion

problem.claim: Long-form, multi-speaker conversational audio generation challenges traditional TTS in scalability, speaker consistency, and natural turn-taking.

gap.claim: Many prior models typically support only 1–2 speakers, limiting multi-speaker podcast synthesis.

contributions.claim: VibeVoice, a zero-shot model for expressive, long-form, multi-speaker speech synthesis.
A continuous speech tokenizer operating at an ultra-low frame rate of 7.5, paired with next-token diffusion.
An annotation pipeline producing pseudo-transcriptions and turn-taking labels from extensive podcast data.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present VibeVoice as a novel model combining efficient continuous speech tokenization, podcast-derived conversational annotations, and next-token diffusion for expressive multi-speaker generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the tokenizer preserves audio fidelity while substantially improving computational efficiency for long sequences.
The authors report synthesis of up to 30 minutes of speech with up to 4 speakers, exceeding the stated typical 1–2-speaker limit of many prior models.
The authors report natural turn-taking and pacing, including subtle non-lexical cues such as breaths and lip smacks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-form multi-speaker podcast generation exposes scalability, speaker-consistency, and turn-taking challenges in traditional TTS.
The authors introduce VibeVoice for zero-shot expressive, long-form speech synthesis with multiple speakers.
The approach uses a 7.5-frame-rate continuous speech tokenizer intended to retain fidelity while reducing long-sequence computation.
Podcast annotations provide pseudo-transcriptions and turn-taking labels, which support next-token diffusion training.
The system is reported to generate up to 30 minutes with up to 4 speakers and to capture conversational timing and non-lexical cues.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a low-rate tokenizer and podcast-specific turn-taking annotations directly to long-form, multi-speaker generation goals.

lessons.interpretation: A strong abstract can connect each major design choice to a named bottleneck and target capability.
lessons.application: When presenting a new system, map each component to a specific scalability, data, or interaction constraint before stating the resulting capability.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when component-to-outcome links are not supported by reported evidence or when the work is primarily theoretical.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide evaluation protocols, baselines, sample counts, or quantitative measures for fidelity, efficiency, naturalness, or turn-taking.
The conditions and meaning of zero-shot synthesis are unspecified.
The comparison with prior models is qualitative; the basis and exact scope of the 1–2-speaker characterization are not detailed.
